messages:
alex: quick heads-up — ran a tiny cross-region hw sweep for embeddings and small-chat (L4 vs T4 vs A10G). posting raw numbers and a few notes, plz react if you want deeper breakdowns :mag_right:
mira: nice, drop the numbers here? curious about p95 and throughput per dollar across regions.
josh: tagging @sophia since she owns the kernel selector and cost model.
mira: ok pasted results below (quick & dirty, 1k requests each region, mixed seq lengths):
```
# embeddings (512-d), batch sizes tuned per device
# format: device | region | p50(ms) | p95(ms) | qps | $/1M tokens equiv (estimate)
L4  | us-east | 18  | 45  | 560  | $42
T4  | us-east | 42  | 120 | 200  | $26
A10G| us-east | 14  | 36  | 740  | $68

L4  | eu-west | 22  | 60  | 480  | $46
T4  | eu-west | 48  | 140 | 180  | $28
A10G| eu-west | 16  | 40  | 670  | $72

L4  | apac    | 26  | 78  | 420  | $55
T4  | apac    | 58  | 170 | 150  | $34
A10G| apac    | 18  | 48  | 600  | $81
```
mira: small-chat (short convs, kv-cache active, seq_len~128):
```
# small-chat, dynamic batching + KV cache warm
L4  | us-east | 28  | 92  | 180  | $90
T4  | us-east | 78  | 260 | 60   | $35
A10G| us-east | 22  | 78  | 240  | $125
```
mira: notes: L4 sits in the middle — best latency/throughput balance for embeddings per-dollar when you care about stable p95. A10G gives raw qps but costs spike; T4 is cheapest per-hour but p95 and tail latency are rough for chat workloads.
sophia: thanks — did you change kernels or quant levels? which cu/kernels used?
mira: default runtime kernels: flash-attn where available, otherwise triton matmul fallback. quant was fp16 for all runs; did a quick int8 quant experiment on embeddings (A10G) and saw ~1.6x throughput, p95 up ~8ms, small quality delta on cosine sims (~0.7% drift).
josh: CV on quant: int8 looked promising for batch-embeddings but for chat with kv-cache int8 increased p95 variance — probably due to dequant/quant hotspots on the decode path.
sophia: kernel note — L4 shows much better fused attention path for seq<=512; that explains the p95 advantage vs T4. A10G we should prefer cuBLAS+fused conv kernels for high-batch embedding runs to hit that qps.
bench-bot: automated note: full logs + perf dumps uploaded to s3://redwood-bench/mini-sweep/1877772468/ (profiles, kernel selection traces, flamegraphs) :package:
alex: cross-region takeaway: if customer cares embeddings cost-first and can tolerate slightly higher p95, T4 in us-east/eu-west is cost-efficient for non-chat. For latency-sensitive chat, prefer L4 or A10G depending on scale (L4 for mid-size pools, A10G if you need max QPS and can absorb cost).
mira: follow-ups: 1) schedule deeper int8 sweep for embeddings (A10G + L4) 2) rerun chat run with mixed-precision decode toggles 3) collect per-request kernel trace for worst p95 samples.
josh: I can take item 3 this week. alex can you create a quick ticket with target SLOs we want to hit?
alex: created ticket #ML-1123 with targets: embeddings p95 < 70ms for eu/us, chat p95 < 100ms for 95% of requests on mid pools. linking in ticket to s3 artifacts.
sophia: will look at kernel selector heuristics — maybe bias to fused kernels for sequences <=512 and prefer fp16 decode for chat.
mira: cool — thanks all. if no objections I'll promote the A10G embedding config to canary in us-east for CustomerX tomorrow morning and monitor cost delta. react :thumbsup: if OK. :rocket:
